writers_instrumented: guest callback interval observations around ExecuteInterrupt
recorded_fields: guest destination and resolved host pointer
register index and decoded register value when applicable
ring generation, batch id, batch RPTR/WPTR, and ring base
source IB, nesting depth, expanded packet ordinal, packet byte offset/type/opcode
active GPU dispatch id, interrupt source/CPU/callback/data, and guest/host thread ids when present
physical and virtual-E guest/host mappings and current values

prior_capture.interpretation: The v65 capture confirms the scratch-register set operation but does not identify the later clear. The wait completing with zero proves the word changed, not which writer changed it.

related_prior_alias_evidence.join_confidence: strong for that v64 run; separate from v65 and not used to label v65 causality
related_prior_alias_evidence.address_correction: The earlier v64 JSON listed guest virtual 0xEB963004, which conflicts with host pointer 0x1FB963004. Current SDK mapping resolves 0xFB963004 to host alias 0x1FB963004 and guest physical 0x1B964004; the corrected F address is used by the instrumentation.

v66_follow_up.prior_bounded_log_saturation: All 64 records were repeated scratch register 0-to-1 writes; the first 1-to-0 change was omitted.
v66_follow_up.new_transition_policy: Discard unchanged observations; reserve independent limits for 64 1-to-0, 8 0-to-1, and 16 other changed-value records.
v66_follow_up.callback_observation: Sample the physical alias and verified virtual-E alias before and after each synchronous ExecuteInterrupt; record callback identity, dispatch ID, CPU, batch, packet, and thread context on a transition.
v66_follow_up.ordinary_guest_cpu_store_hook: None in the plugin API. ReXGlue exposes page/cache invalidation access callbacks, not an exact per-store callback. Callback interval sampling observes changes within ExecuteInterrupt but does not identify an individual CPU store instruction.

limits: This follow-up artifact has not yet been replayed against the retail game; use the same-XEX run to test whether a 1-to-0 transition occurs inside a guest callback interval.
The v64 virtual-alias writer identifies the analogous clear in that run, but does not establish the v65 writer.
Callback interval sampling may observe a concurrent write occurring during the callback; P1 GDB is still required to identify an exact CPU store instruction.
This is a Linux x86-64 diagnostic artifact, not an Android ARM64 build.
